kept.title: Arbitrary File Disclosure via Include Directive
kept.description: The `Include` directive in `src/mistune/directives/include.py` allows arbitrary file inclusion from the filesystem. While it attempts to check common path roots, it relies on `os.path.realpath` and `os.path.commonpath`, which can be bypassed via symlink attacks or specific OS-level path configurations to access sensitive files outside the intended directory.
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious markdown file that uses the .. include:: directive.
Target a sensitive file (e.g., /etc/passwd or configuration files) using path traversal.
The parser reads and includes the content of the file directly into the rendered output.
kept.impact: An attacker can read any file on the server accessible by the process running the application.

kept.title: Unsafe Output Handling in CLI Tool
kept.description: The command line interface in `src/mistune/__main__.py` accepts an `--output` argument and opens that file for writing. This allows an attacker to overwrite any file on the system that the current user has write access to.
steps_to_exploit: Run the mistune CLI tool.
Use the --output flag with a path to a critical system file (e.g., ~/.bashrc or a config file).
The tool writes rendered Markdown content into the target file, potentially leading to command injection or system instability.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file write leading to privilege escalation or service disruption.

kept.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in HTML Rendering
kept.description: The `HTMLRenderer` in `src/mistune/renderers/html.py` has an `escape` flag that, if disabled (which is common in many configurations), allows arbitrary HTML tags. Combined with custom directives like `Admonition`, user-provided input can inject scripts.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a site using mistune where `escape=false` is enabled.
Submit a markdown snippet containing malicious HTML/JS (e.g., `<script>alert(1)</script>`).
The script executes in the victim's browser context.
kept.impact: Unauthorized script execution, session hijacking, or defacement of the application.

kept.title: Potential Path Traversal in Image Directive
kept.description: The Image directive in `src/mistune/directives/image.py` does not perform sufficient validation on the `target` parameter provided in the directive, which is then passed to `escape_url` and subsequently used in rendered HTML.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a directive containing a `target` attribute that points to a malicious URL.
The rendered HTML creates a link pointing to this destination.
This facilitates phishing or open redirect vulnerabilities if the target is external.
kept.impact: Open redirect or phishing attacks targeting users.

kept.title: Plugin Import Injection
kept.description: The `import_plugin` function in `src/mistune/plugins/__init__.py` uses `import_module` with a string derived from the user input. If an attacker can influence the plugin list passed to `create_markdown`, they can force the loading of arbitrary python modules.
steps_to_exploit: Find an entry point where an attacker-controlled string is used to specify plugins.
Pass a path to a different python module (e.g., `os` or `subprocess`).
The application imports the specified module.
kept.impact: Arbitrary code execution if an attacker can load a module with side-effect code.

kept.title: ReDoS in URL Pattern
kept.description: The `URL_LINK_PATTERN` in `src/mistune/plugins/url.py` is susceptible to catastrophic backtracking if it encounters a specially crafted URL, as it does not bound the search or validate the input effectively.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a string consisting of thousands of characters that trigger exponential backtracking.
The CPU spikes to 100% processing the regex.
The service becomes unresponsive to other users.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via resource exhaustion.

kept.title: ReDoS in Math Directive Pattern
kept.description: The `BLOCK_MATH_PATTERN` in `src/mistune/plugins/math.py` uses non-greedy matching on large inputs that could lead to regex engine timeout or performance degradation.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a large block of text starting with `$$` but lacking a closing `$$`.
The parser consumes excessive memory and CPU time trying to find the end match.
The application performance degrades.

kept.title: Use of unsafe `pickle` alternative (Logic)
kept.description: The caching mechanism in `src/mistune/__init__.py` caches the `Markdown` instance keyed by the `plugins` argument. This cache uses in-memory dicts, but if the plugin list contains complex or non-hashable types, it might cause runtime errors or unexpected behavior.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a complex, mutable object or non-hashable list as a plugin argument.
The application crashes due to a `TypeError` during cache lookup.
Service failure.
kept.impact: Application denial of service or unexpected runtime state.

kept.title: Missing Input Sanitization in Admonition Title
kept.description: In `src/mistune/directives/admonition.py`, the `render_admonition_title` function does not sanitize the `text` attribute before rendering, potentially leading to XSS if the title is user-controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Create an admonition with a malicious title string containing HTML tags.
Render the document as HTML.
The malicious script is injected into the HTML title.

kept.title: Insecure Protocol Handling
kept.description: The `HTMLRenderer.safe_url` in `src/mistune/renderers/html.py` uses `_unquote_url` to decode input before checking against `SAFE_PROTOCOLS`. If an attacker double-encodes a forbidden protocol, the security check might be bypassed.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL using double-encoded malicious protocol (e.g., `javascript:alert(1)` encoded).
Pass this URL to a link or image directive.
The check `_unquote_url` potentially decodes it after the check or confuses the logic.

kept.title: Unbounded Recursion in List Parser
kept.description: The list parser in `src/mistune/list_parser.py` lacks strict recursion depth control when parsing deeply nested lists, leading to potential `RecursionError`.
steps_to_exploit: Create a markdown file with hundreds of levels of nested list items.
The recursive parser consumes all stack space.
The application crashes.

kept.title: Insecure File Read with Uncontrolled Encoding
kept.description: The `Include` directive in `src/mistune/directives/include.py` allows the user to specify an encoding for the included file. Providing an unexpected encoding can lead to misinterpretation of content.
steps_to_exploit: Define an include directive with an exotic encoding attribute.
The file is read and decoded using the specified encoding, potentially misinterpreting content or revealing info based on character conversion errors.
kept.impact: Information disclosure or bypass of downstream security filters.

kept.title: XSS in Block Error Rendering
kept.description: The `block_error` renderer in `src/mistune/renderers/html.py` renders error messages. If these messages contain unescaped user-input content, an attacker might inject malicious HTML.
steps_to_exploit: Force a parsing error that displays part of the input in the error message.
The error message reflects the malicious HTML back to the page.
Script executes.

kept.title: Unvalidated `attrs` in Figure Renderer
kept.description: The `render_figure` function in `src/mistune/directives/image.py` accepts custom CSS classes and widths without strict sanitization.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a malicious CSS class name into the directive attribute.
The rendered HTML contains the malicious attribute, which may impact style or facilitate further injection if combined with other vulnerabilities.

kept.title: Information Leak via Debug Error Messages
kept.description: The TableOfContents directive in `src/mistune/directives/toc.py` raises `ValueError` with specific information about the user input. In some production configurations, these exceptions might be displayed directly to the end-user.
steps_to_exploit: Provide invalid levels (e.g., non-integers) in the TOC directive.
Observe the error message containing internal application constraints.
Use this information to fingerprint the application's configuration or logic.
